items: T5 Judgment — Confirm affected-file prior art across merged history and closed/rejected work before sign-off — this disposable target has one synthetic commit and no remotes, so the brief's prior-attempt claims cannot be independently reproduced and overlapping earlier work could change the judgment (`brief.md:284`).
**The `pending:` writers still accept an owned or torn entry.**
C4 per-fix red->green: this patch's test red pre-fix, green post-fix unverifiable —                why this slice has no isolable red (the cargo output is above).

T5 Judgment — Confirm prior-art overlap against the current base for every affected path — the supplied check is anchored to older `origin/main` evidence and selected shared files, while this disposable target has one commit and no remotes, so merged or closed stacked work could change the conflict and scope judgment (`brief.md:284`).

T4 is a gating check and it is still red, with two blockers (`gate-logs/T4-batch-review.log`): no seeded Tier-0 DST (deterministic simulation test) coverage for the changed sweep at `crates/core/src/write.rs:654` or the GC skip at `crates/custodian/src/gc.rs:502`. The finding is accurate. Before the patch, one unreadable `pending:` value aborted the whole pass. Now both sweeps keep going and delete other entries, and the rubric's *Test fidelity* rule asks for seeded DST coverage of that kind of change. The brief rules it out, though: `crates/dst/tests/custodian.rs` may only get the mechanical initializer, and a 14th file means STOP. The existing DST leg (`crates/dst/tests/custodian.rs:883`) seeds only ordinary leases. A rebuild can't clear this without breaking the brief. A human has to choose: record a rejection reason (the rubric's "Definition of done"), or widen scope, e.g. a follow-up issue for a seeded leg with misfiled, torn and garbage `pending:` values.

The brief's S8 negation can't work as written. "Remove ONE `skip_serializing_if` … on the owned witness" has no effect on an owned value, because both fields are `Some`. I removed the attribute from `owner` (`crates/core/src/metadata.rs:1601`): S7 (`crates/core/tests/multipart_owned_staging.rs:638`) failed and S8 (`:662`) **passed**. What S8 actually guards is the `sidx:` canonical-bytes check: dropping `require_canonical` at `crates/core/src/multipart.rs:3627` fails S8 and only S8. So the eight-negation evidence holds with that swap. But `build-notes.md` (withheld from me) should record the canonical-gate negation for S8. If it says the briefed negation failed S8, that claim is wrong.
